- Chat: self-hosted/gpt-oss-120b (overridden to the value of LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL)
- Embedding: self-hosted/bge-m3 (overridden to LITELLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL, 1024 dimensions)
- Vision: some VLM model (overridden to LITELLM_VISUAL_MODEL)

So my local LLM endpoint just needs to accept whatever model name I write into .env (since process-compose forces all model variables to .env values). E.g., I could use:
- LITELLM_TEXT_MODEL=local-chat
- LITELLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL=local-embed
- LITELLM_VISUAL_MODEL=local-vision

And my stub server accepts any model name.

- GET /health
- GET /v1/models
- POST /v1/chat/completions (non-streaming + streaming)
- POST /v1/embeddings (1024 dimensions, deterministic)
- POST /v1/audio/transcriptions probably unnecessary

The services might also call the OpenAI SDK's `/chat/completions`. Some might use the `/responses` API? Let me check which client is used: litellm, openai python, httpx. The OpenAI python SDK v1.x defaults to the /chat/completions endpoint. Newer SDKs might use /responses for the responses API, but only when explicitly requested. Let me check if there's any usage of "responses.create" in the codebase.

Also, the vision model: modul-inhaltsextraktion uses VLLM_MODEL for page analysis. The stub just needs to accept it.

Additionally, the injection model: `INJECTION_MODEL_URL=http://localhost:18001` — points to DMS? Interesting; INJECTION_LLM_SCAN_ENABLED=false disables this, so it's fine.
